# What it is

[isoLASER](https://github.com/gxiaolab/isoLASER) — *isoform-Level Analysis of
Allele-Specific processing of Exonic Regions*. Quinones-Valdez, Amoah & Xiao,
[*Nat Commun* 16:9603 (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6).

It is the planned method for aim 2 (genetic variants associated with splicing).
Three steps in one tool:

1. **De novo variant calling** from the long reads — scAllele-based de Bruijn
   local reassembly, then a multi-layer perceptron to filter false positives.
2. **Gene-level phasing** — weighted k-means over read-level alleles,
   **K = 2, assuming one diploid genome**. Simultaneously phases variants and
   haplotags reads.
3. **Linkage testing** between haplotype and exonic-part inclusion, scored by
   adjusted mutual information (AMI).

Events are classified **cis-directed** (AMI above the 99th percentile of a
simulated null, plus |delta PSI| >= 5%), **trans-directed** (below the 95th),
or ambiguous. `isolaser_joint` merges >= 2 samples to call splicing-associated
variants (SAVs) and can reach rare variants.

The appeal for this project: it requires neither a pre-phased genome nor a VCF,
and works at small sample sizes — the paper frames it explicitly as an
alternative to sQTL mapping. Their SAVs replicated against GTEx sQTLs
(delta PSI vs sQTL beta, R = -0.37).

## Pitfalls hit during install

- **`conda create` appeared to hang for >10 min.** It was *not* the solver
  (libmamba solves in seconds) — it was the "Executing transaction" stage
  writing thousands of small files to the shared `/home` filesystem. Do not
  pipe conda through `tail`, or you see no progress and may kill a job that is
  nearly finished. Expect ~10 min.
- **The system Python 3.8** (`/software/python-3.8.5-el8-x86_64/bin/python3`)
  fails with `libpython3.8.so.1.0: cannot open shared object file` unless you
  set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/software/python-3.8.5-el8-x86_64/lib`. Avoided by using
  conda instead of a venv.
- A container fallback exists if the env ever breaks
  (`singularity pull library://giovas/collection/s6`); modules
  `apptainer/1.4.1` and `singularity/3.9.2` are available.

## Which reference to use

The IsoQuant GTF at `data/reference/OUT.extended_annotation.gtf` records the
original command line in its header, which names the reference explicitly:

```
-r .../refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A/fasta/genome.fa
-g .../refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A/genes/genes.gtf
```

That is the **10x Cell Ranger GRCh38 2024-A** bundle, publicly downloadable and
shipping an indexed `genome.fa`. Use that one — not the Ensembl v112 GTF that
was used as a stopgap for early QC, which is a different annotation with
different coordinates and IDs.

# The blocker that matters most

**isoLASER assumes bulk, single-donor long-read RNA-seq. Our BAM is pooled
single-cell across >= 2 donors.** Phasing fixes K = 2 on the assumption of one
diploid genome, so running it directly on all 8,612 cells would be meaningless.

Required order:

> demultiplex donors (vireo / souporcell) -> pseudobulk per donor ->
> `isolaser` per donor -> `isolaser_joint` across donors

So **installation is not on the critical path — donor demultiplexing is.**

A second concern to quantify before committing: isoLASER needs a heterozygous
SNP **and** the splicing event on the *same read*, and its pipeline discards
reads lacking splice junctions. With our ~506 bp median read and 27% spliced
fraction, testable events per donor will be well below what the full-length
PacBio data the method was built on yields.

Also, the paper's own ONT guidance: exclude indels and validate variants
against gnomAD before phasing. Our median error (~1.1%) is better than the
R9.4.1 data they used, but the advice still applies.

# How it is run

From the README, with our paths. Not yet executed on project data.

## Preprocessing

```bash
# 1. transcriptome fasta from the GTF
isolaser_convert_gtf_to_fasta -g {annot.gtf} -f {genome.fa} -o {transcriptome}

# 2. re-align reads to that transcriptome (this is what needs minimap2)
samtools fastq {input.bam} > {input.fq}
minimap2 -t 16 -ax splice:hq -uf --MD {transcriptome.fa} {input.fq} > {transcriptome.sam}

# 3. annotate the BAM with ZG (gene) and ZT (transcript) tags,
#    dropping secondary/supplementary and trans-gene reads
isolaser_annotate -b {input.bam} -t {transcriptome.sam} -g {annot.gtf} -o {input.annot}

# 4. exonic parts database (one pickle per gene)
isolaser_extract_exon_parts -g {annot.gtf} -o {transcript.db}
```

## Single sample

```bash
isolaser -b {input.annot.bam} -o {prefix} -t {transcript.db} -f {genome.fa}
# -> {prefix}.vcf, {prefix}.mi_summary.tsv

sort -k1,1V -k2,2n -k3,3n {prefix}.mi_summary.tsv | bgzip -c -f > {prefix}.mi_summary.tsv.gz
tabix -f -p bed {prefix}.mi_summary.tsv.gz

isolaser_filter -m {prefix}.mi_summary.tsv.gz -o {prefix}.mi_summary.filtered.tsv.gz
```

## Joint across samples

`fofn.tsv` lists one sample per line:

```
SM1  SM1.mi_summary.tsv.gz  SM1.gvcf
SM2  SM2.mi_summary.tsv.gz  SM2.gvcf
```

```bash
isolaser_combine_vcf -i fofn.tsv -o {prefix} -f {genome.fa}   # wraps GATK
isolaser_joint -i fofn.tsv -o {prefix} -t {transcript.db} -v {prefix}.genotyped.vcf
# -> {prefix}.merged.mi_summary.tsv
```

## Validating the install

`software/isoLASER/test_pipeline/` ships three DLPFC BAMs, expected outputs,
and a Snakemake workflow. It is self-contained — no genome FASTA or project
data needed — so it is the right way to confirm the install end to end:

```bash
cd /project/xinhe/xsun/long_read_RNA/software/isoLASER/test_pipeline
snakemake -s isolaser_test.smk
```
